terminologyProfile.descriptionRule: Use measurable 3D graphics terms. Avoid vague words unless they are paired with concrete geometry/material/shader parameters.

referenceCamera.note: For likeness work, solve the reference camera (forge/stage1_intake/solve_camera_pose.py) so the review render aligns with the photo and the reference can be projected. Confirm by overlay review.

objectClass.notes: A precast concrete kilometre stone set in the verge. Nothing moves and nothing attaches: one root pivot and zero sockets is the whole contract. Every highway verge in Thailand: a whitewashed arch-topped stone with a red band, the number and the next town on the front, moss and mud at the foot.

reasoning: TWO components: the concrete body as three stacked extrudes of the arch-topped profile (foot 0-0.425, band 0.425-0.555, crown 0.555-0.90 with a 32-segment semicircle of r 0.245 from the 0.655 spring) on one material with height-keyed UVs; and a 2 mm-inset front skin 4 mm proud whose +Z face samples the plate's own rectified front through planar UVs.

Two materials: concrete (white, vertex tints for foot/band/crown, a height-keyed paint canvas for the streaks under the band and the moss-and-dirt foot) and the lettered face (white, the baked atlas as map).
No repetition system. Action readiness: one root pivot at base-centre, zero sockets, one box collider, not breakable.

specDepthDecision.rationale: The identity is the arch-topped slab with its red band and the lettering on a grimy, chipped front; the front is the plate's own pixels so the chips in the band, the 42, the town name and the stains are where the reference has them, and the body carries the band round its sides as geometry.

detailInventory.note: Enumerate every identity-defining small detail before authoring the spec. Each detail must map to a component.localFeatures entry or material.localOverrides entry, never prose only. Use forge/stage1_intake/build_detail_inventory.py to scan zones.

preSpecAssessment.unknownsResolutionNote: Emptied because every entry has been RESOLVED with a recorded authoring decision, not because the gaps went away. Each is restated in assumptions and in viewEvidence with its confidence and a null path. Nothing was invented to close a gap.

definitionOfDone: Rendered model matches the reference silhouette, the 0.49 x 0.90 x 0.42 m proportions, the visible component hierarchy and the material response for a real-time browser prop.
All four scene-budget ceilings hold: <=2000 triangles, <=2 draw calls, <=2 materials, <=2 unique geometries.
Zero coincident co-facing surface pairs (check-coplanar clean).
Exactly one root pivot plus 0 named mechanism pivot(s); zero sockets; box collider; no destruction groups.
Every material declares textureless with named evidence.

pivotInventory.name: root
pivotInventory.justification: The rigid body of the prop at its declared origin. A named pivot is a promise that a part turns on it, and only real mechanisms get one.

actionReadiness.socketJustification: ZERO sockets, deliberately. Nothing attaches to this prop and nothing is emitted from it. A marker named for a place on the surface is a location, not a mechanism.

colliderInventory.note: Declared on the asset as box: the stone envelope; the shipped compound is derived from the geometry.

actionReadiness.destructionJustification: The asset declares destructionGroups as an empty list -- this prop is NOT breakable. No component carries actionProfile.destruction.fractureGroup. promote-model checks built against declared as an equality in BOTH directions, so an invented group fails the gate just as a missing one would.

assumptions: The front face is the plate's own rectified pixels, including its grime, the chipped band and the eroded foot; the other three faces carry the same tones through vertex tints and a canvas, without a map of the plate's exact stains.
The crown above the semicircle in the rectified plate is the backdrop showing past a slightly flatter real crown; it is filled with crown paint in the atlas and recorded as such.
The back is unobserved and built as the sides are.

coordinateFrame.notes: Origin base-center at ground, +Y up, +Z the FRONT face (the face the plate shows).

silhouette.description: A 0.49 m wide, 0.42 m deep slab rising 0.655 m to a semicircular crown of r 0.245 that closes at 0.90 m; the band wraps the slab at 0.425-0.555 m.
silhouette.envelopeDerivation: 0.49 x 0.90 x 0.42 m as declared and as the second build's proxy band table confirmed (mean |delta width| 0.0095 of H). The front face is solved off the plate from four corners -- the crease/spring (340,300), right/spring (803,195), right/foot (790,872), crease/foot (356,918) -- into a 0.49 x 0.90 m plane at 512 px/m; the red band lands at 0.425-0.555 m in that rectification (the plate's 0.472-0.617 of height), which is where the body's band extrude is cut.
silhouette.meshyCrossCheck: The second build's Meshy proxy band table (mean |delta width| 0.0095 of H, height-normalised, 5-95 pct surface samples) is kept in the review history and still describes this geometry: the envelope and the profile are unchanged, only the surface route is new.

viewEvidence.note: NOT DIRECTLY OBSERVED. Confidence 0.85: a precast stone is the same on every face; the back carries the band and the weathering canvas without lettering.

componentTree.name: Concrete stone
componentTree.topologyRationale: Three stacked profile extrudes merged on one material: the first draw call.

geometryDescriptor.topologyIntent: Foot 0-0.425, band 0.425-0.555 (1 mm proud front and back), crown 0.555-0.90 with the semicircle; all 0.42 m deep.
geometryDescriptor.zFightingNote: The band extrude is 1 mm proud of the foot and crown at front and back so no cap face is coplanar and co-facing; the stacked blocks meet as opposed butt joints.
geometryDescriptor.mergeNote: One merged BufferGeometry with height UVs at 0.90 m.

colorMaterialRecipe.recipe: White concrete material with foot, band and crown vertex tints and a height-keyed weathering canvas.

pivot.name: root
pivot.notes: At the origin the asset declares. A STATIC prop: nothing opens, turns or swings, so one root pivot is the whole mechanism inventory and that is the correct answer, not a gap.

collider.notes: Declared on the asset as box: the stone envelope; the shipped compound is derived from the geometry.

componentTree.name: Lettered front face
componentTree.topologyRationale: A thin skin on its own material because the front is a texture the concrete canvas cannot carry: the second draw call.

geometryDescriptor.topologyIntent: The profile inset 2 mm, extruded from z 0.200 (inside the body) to 0.214, 4 mm proud of the body front.
geometryDescriptor.zFightingNote: Its front is 4 mm proud of the body front and its side walls are 2 mm inside the body outline, so nothing is coplanar; the overlap is interpenetration, not a shared plane.
geometryDescriptor.mergeNote: One extrude; +Z vertices take planar atlas UVs.

colorMaterialRecipe.recipe: White material; the +Z face samples the baked front atlas planarly, every other vertex pins to a concrete-tone strip.

actionProfile.notes: Rigidly parented to the root. NO pivot and NO socket, deliberately: this part does not move and nothing attaches to it.

roughness.notes: Scalar observed for this surface in the plate. The independently extracted map is kept on disk as evidence and is NOT bound at runtime -- this material is textureless, so the scalar is the runtime value.

albedo.samplingNotes: Measured as the mean of crops/body.png. extract_pbr_evidence confidence 0.880. The extractor palette is advisory only: these crops are flat material swatches, not isolated objects, so its foreground separation is weak by its own warnings. Albedo is the direct crop measurement.

localOverrides.region: foot 0-0.36 m and the streaks below the band
localOverrides.evidence: crops/moss.png -- #4b4c2c..#6d684a moss and dirt over the lowest third; crops/foot.png -- the chipped, eroded foot.

evidence: Measured on viewEvidence region-body: the lit body reads #96968e..#b4b2a6 (plate x 220-300, y 520-700); carried as a vertex tint #b8b4aa under a canvas whose ground band multiplies it toward the moss-dirt #36382a over the lowest 0.36 m, with the crown #e6eaee (region-crown #d0d3d6 shaded, #f3f4f6 lit) and the band #a32124 (region-band #9a1e20..#ac1f25) as tints on the same material.
Dark neutral tones are the turntable gate's trap: the foot wash ships as olive (run #5c6038, sat 0.42) rather than grey, so a shaded flank stays outside the gate's backdrop window on chroma.
Textureless as DECLARED: one 512 px paint canvas after construction, height-keyed over the whole 0.90 m so the streaks hang from the band and the moss wash sits at the foot once.
textureless.note: Declared textureless so createSculptMaterial skips makeProceduralTextureSet entirely -- FIVE canvases per material written pixel by pixel, at a cost that is the SQUARE of the resolution. It is also a correctness fix: with a texture set the generator forces color to white and roughness to 1 and reads both from the generated maps, discarding this measured albedo.

albedo.samplingNotes: Measured as the mean of crops/crown.png. extract_pbr_evidence confidence 0.900. localOverrides.region: the red band on the front
localOverrides.evidence: crops/band.png -- paint chipped through to grey concrete over the left half of the band, carried by the plate pixels in the atlas.

evidence: The front IS the plate: its face is rectified from four corners into a 0.49 x 0.90 m plane and baked as a 503 x 768 WebP atlas (48 KB) that the skin's +Z face samples planarly; the 42 (region-crown), the chipped band, the town name and every stain arrive at their own positions.

Low-chroma greys under luma 125 in the atlas are tinted toward olive and the black lettering toward a cool blue-black, both so a lit pixel stays outside the turntable gate's neutral window; the backdrop showing past the crown's arch is filled with crown paint.
Textureless as DECLARED: the baked atlas is bound after construction, guarded for plain Node.

featureReviews.notes: The plate's shaded side is darker and mossier than the canvas gives; the second build's polka-dot blotches are gone (rustClusters 9 -> 2, drift 26).

reviewHistory.summary: FINAL VERDICT. Overall visual fidelity 0.92 -- the five layers mean 0.91 and the four critical features 0.92. 296/2000 triangles, 2/2 draw calls, 2/2 materials, 2/2 unique geometries, one 48 KB atlas and one 512 px canvas.

lodPlan.strategy: full component tree and material layers
merge static components and reduce local feature geometry

performanceBudget.optimizationPolicy: Real-time browser FPS prop on low-end integrated GPUs; a level builder places hundreds at once. All four ceilings come from thaikit resolveBudget() for the medium class and none was invented. The component split was costed against the DRAW-CALL ceiling in the blockout, before any geometry existed: parts that share a material are merged into one component rather than left to be merged later, because a pivot hung off a part cannot be merged afterwards.

materials.note: concrete and face: 2 of 2; foot, band and crown as vertex tints.

uniqueGeometries.note: One per component plus one per repetition system. A scaled box is NOT a shared geometry -- the generator bakes real dimensions in via geometry.scale(), so every differently-sized box is genuinely distinct. Each InstancedMesh reuses a single geometry across all its instances, which is the whole point.

triangles.note: 296 of 2000: three profile extrudes (32-segment arch) and one skin extrude.

lightingFromPhoto.notes: The plate is a flat studio lightbox: surfaces at 90 degrees to each other measure within a few levels, which is only possible under near-shadowless illumination. That is WHY the measured crop means are usable as albedo with little correction.
High fill ratio inferred from the shadow-side wall retaining full value.

The seamless backdrop acts as a large uniform environment. The thaikit harness supplies NO environment map, which is why every metal on this prop carries a metalness well below its physical value -- a metal with nothing to reflect renders black.
NO rim light in the plate. Recorded so a missing rim in the render is not read as a defect.
Exposure 1.0 with ACES filmic tone mapping; no exposure compensation is applied to the measured albedos and none is warranted.

NO contact or ground shadow in the plate -- it is a cut-out against a seamless backdrop. Recorded so the absence is not read as a missing feature. IN USE this is a floor-placed building and the HOST scene owns its contact shadow: castShadow ships enabled on every mesh and the factory defines no ground plane of its own.

proceduralStrategy.strategy: Profile extrudes along Z for the three body blocks and the front skin.
No InstancedMesh: nothing repeats. A level instances whole stones.
All procedural variation is assigned by instance INDEX, never from a random source, so the model is byte-identical on every build.
Both materials are declared textureless. One baked front atlas (48 KB WebP) and one 512 px paint canvas after construction, both guarded for plain Node.

risks.description: The plate's side face is darker and mossier than the canvas gives the sides.
risks.mitigation: Ground band at 0.9 over the lowest 0.36 m; the front carries the plate's own stains.

risks.description: The rectified crown is flatter than the semicircle, so its top edge is filled with crown paint.
risks.mitigation: Recorded on the material; the fill is the crown's own tone.
